_comment: Registry for the Parakeet ops dashboard.
The Property Data Sheet decides WHO appears: a community is on the dashboard only
if `vwr VW_PDS_V2` marks it Reportable = Yes (exported to raw/pds_reportable.json).
That replaced a pile of inferred rules about x-prefixes, duplicate ledgers and fund
entities, all of which the Reportable flag settles correctly on its own.
What is left here is the handful of things the PDS does not encode:
sold       - dispositions the PDS has not caught up with yet
roll_up    - sub-ledgers that bill against a reportable parent's lots
segments   - MH/RV splits of one physical park
unit_types - vacancy composition and the occupancy denominator
Every name the warehouse returns lands in data/registry_audit.json with its
disposition, so anything newly reportable or newly missing shows up there.
_grace_day_comment: Rent bills on the 1st. After this day, unpaid current-month charges are late.
_sold_comment: Excluded even while the PDS still reads Reportable = Yes, because a disposition
lands in the PDS later than it lands in reality. Austin confirmed both entries
The build raises an informational flag for any entry here that is still marked
Reportable, so the override stays visible and can be retired once the PDS catches
up: flip Reportable to No and fill the Sale Date, then delete the entry here.
To re-include a property, delete its entry.
_roll_up_comment: Sub-ledgers that carry real receivables and GL activity but bill against lots
already counted on a reportable parent. Their money attributes to the parent and
their unit counts are ignored; the build reports the rolled-in total as a flag.
A roll_up whose parent is not Reportable = Yes is dropped instead.
_segments_comment: Physical parks the PDS splits across two reportable records. They stay separate
rows but share a `park` so portfolio views can group them.
